items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: And his name was Ray Nance. He was quite an inspiration to us

ctx.x: Oh yeah. You just started to talk about Danny Thomas.

Oh yes. That was in the 5100 Club in Chicago, and I had a big band then. There was a fellow there that played the violin and the trumpet. And his name was Ray Nance. He was quite an inspiration to us, and he was always a salesman. A Chicago boy. And Duke Ellington came to town and heard Ray. (Inaudible). He loved Ray and wanted Ray to join him. You know, Ray didn't want to leave the band? He wanted to stay with us, and I had to get mad with Ray. Ray will tell anybody this, and finally, we showed him where it…
You know, my brother began to write more and more for Benny Goodman around this time.
